Titan Quest: Anniversary Edition — Mein kurzer Kriegsbericht

Legendär? Ja. Frustrierend? Auch ja.

Was mir NICHT gefällt

- Steuerung fühlt sich oft wie ein alter Ochse an: träge und ungenau.
- Nahkampf-Targeting: Gegner werden nur angegriffen, wenn man sie einzeln und genau anklickt — sonst steht der Charakter nur rum und lässt sich verprügeln.
- Loot für Nahkämpfer: schlechte Droprate. Mein Eroberer steht öfter mit leeren Händen da als ein Tourist ohne Reiseführer.
- Typhon (Fluch der Götter): völlig übertrieben stark — vor allem gegen Nahkämpfer. Sein Lebensraub macht jeden Fortschritt zunichte.
- Nostalgie‑Vergleich: Vor 20 Jahren war Typhon ebenfalls hart, aber noch fair — heute fühlt es sich eher nach „Unfaire Gottheit 2.0“ an.

Was gut ist

+ Immer noch ein legendäres Spiel. (Ich hab’s vor rund 20 Jahren geliebt.)

Warum ich am Ende den Daumen gesenkt habe
Ich spiele einen Eroberer auf Normal — ein kerniger Nahkämpfer. Logisch das nur Stärke und Geschick erhöht wird. Doch fast alle brauchbaren Items verlangen Intelligenz. Ergebnis: Loot‑Frust deluxe. Ich bin Stufe 37, habe bisher nur drei nutzbare Nahkampfwaffen gefunden — der Rest war Müll (inklusive des berüchtigten Säbelzahns: nach 1.000 getöteten Tigermännern einmal gefunden und war nur für die Tonne). Bosskämpfe? Klar, die gibt's, nur keinen Loot - bessere Ausrüstung fand ich öfter in Knochenhaufen.

Steuerung & QoL‑Ärger

Gegner werden nur bei direkten Anklicken bekämpft — ich hab mir ein Mausklick‑Makro angelegt, sonst würde der Kämpfer die halbe Zeit nur rumstehen und einstecken.
Drops kommen in Zeitlupe; oft habe ich grüne Gegenstände gefunden, wenn ich nochmal zurück gegangen bin und nachgeschaut habe.
Die Karte ist irreführend: sieht aus, als gäbe es noch unentdeckte Wege — aber nein, Dead End. Verwirrend und nervig.

Mein Höhepunkt des Frusts: Typhon - Fluch der Götter im Olymp
Der Eroberer ist Stufe 37, ~3700 Leben, über 500 Schaden — hilft alles nicht. Wenn man mühevoll den Gesundheitsbalken gekürzt hat saugt Typhon mir Leben ab und heilt sich damit. Als Nahkämpfer ist das kaum zu umgehen. Oder man startet einen Angriff und er fährt seine Stacheln aus, dann muss man sich schnell heilen oder man ist tot... mal wieder. Das fühlt sich weniger wie spannender Endkampf und mehr wie zähes Glücksspiel an. Spaßfaktor: unterirdisch.

Fazit (kurz)
Titan Quest AE hat noch den alten Charme, aber Balance und QoL‑Probleme — speziell für Nahkämpfer — machen das Spielen an einigen Stellen frustrierend. Wenn man nostalgische Gefühle pflegt, lohnt sich ein Blick; wer aber flüssiges Looten und faire Bosskämpfe will, braucht etwas anderes: GRIM DAWN

The "I've played 2k hours to Age of Mythology" average experience. 

While my frieds were playing Diablo 2 and Diablo 3 I was killing telkines and stuff.
If you've played Grim Dawn this is kind of its grandpa. When THQ (TQ's Devs) got broke like 15 years ago, some of the devs founded Crate Entertainment, and developed Grim Dawn. 

So this Titan Quest will have a lot of stuff Grim Dawn will polish. Like Demon's Souls and Dark Souls, being this one a polishment of Demon's Souls experience. 

So I mean double mastery (classes), and the same core mechanics.
While GD is a more modern approach TQ still has the sh*t old school ARPG had: Secrets and easter eggs.
I've played a lot of Grim Dawn (and with a friend's Steam Account on which he had all 3 expansions I got over 1.5k hours in) and I still discover new stuff every playthrough. 
That's almost the same thing with TQ, I had the game physically ages ago and I bought Anniversary Edition because of the lanuch of ANOTHER expansion (Eternal Embers) for the very endgame and the last difficulty. 

And still there's stuff I've just never seen in the game. 
100% recommended for a classic ARPG experience. If you don't want to pay a lot for other ARPGs and you're not comfortable with D2 (even resurrected HD version) this can be a good substitute.

The story is quite simple, some mythological sh*t (Telkine) are trying to free some random titans (Like Age of Mythology xd) and with spell and sword you must save the day. 
Base game (Base game + Expansion) will take you from ancient Greece, to Egypt, then Babilonic hanging gardens (one of the 8 wonders of ancient world) and the mystic steppes of China, including the Great Wall. And then, even Mount Olympus where gods live. Also you can visit the underworld and even fight against Hades himself. 

The Anniversary Edition includes Atlantis optional expansion (No need to say where you'll travel to xd), Ragnarok (also, pretty self-explanatory) and Eternal Embers, the last one, traveling back to ancient China, with expanded mythology playable areas.

The thing is you must go through 3 difficulties (normal -> epic -> legendary) with resistance underscalling (-30% -> -60%) and improve your gear and character. 

The only downside I've found is there's some multiplayer-related achievements I had to cheese with a couple friends. So the game's imposible to 100% alone. 
Besides that or if you're not interested on 100% your Steam Library, it's still an awesome game even in big 2026 when I wrote this review. 

Grim Dawn's better, for sure, but this one is a very very solid option.

Very fun game, though other people have listed similar complaints I have
-Random crashes out of the blue which can put you back some distance to the last revive point you attuned at.

-Loot tables are crazy stingy. I was on the final act of the main game before I finally found an upgrade to the boots I bought off the vendor in Athens in the First Act. So unless you're willing to look up the wiki for things you want and dedicate a hard set amount of time for a .10% drop rate, or download a community mod to boost the drop rates of uncommons and rares, you're better off making the best of what you get.

-Despite it being the anniversary edition, they 'still' haven't increased the storage capacity: making it so you 'still' have to rely on mule characters like the '06 release when your storage starts filling up, nor have they added a system to search and sort; making sifting through the heaps of relics you'll be picking up a tedious chore at times.

Looking past my complaints, I really do enjoy this game. The dual skill tree aspect makes for fun class combos. The setting is a pleasant change of pace compared to most other Diablo-likes on the market that are just dark and brooding, Titan Quest flips the script with bright and gorgeous scenery that still holds up to this day, with a lot of diverse biomes and regions, along with a lot of enemy diversity throughout the Acts that keeps the game feeling fresh.

Overall, I give the game a solid 7.5, you get a lot of content for $20 dollars between the base game and the Immortal Throne DLC that comes baked into the anniversary edition. I'd go on a limb and give an 8 considering I'm actually 'playing' more, rather than sitting in the hub looking through a wall of suffixes and affixes to determine if a ring is 1% better than the one I'm currently wearing. (Looking at you, Diablo 4..)

I've had some fun playing this game. Yet, I've left a recommendation of "No". There are many reasons for this. For frame of reference, I've got around 1300+ hours in POE, 1000+ in the Diablo series, finished Torchlight 1 & 2 multiple times, played through Grim Dawn twice, and I've forgotten what else. Here are a few of my reasons for not recommending this game (at least to friends).

Inventory is possibly the worst of all the ARPG type games I've ever played. It's a huge annoyance at the best of times. Although I did appreciate that you can purchase a small amount of extra space in your stash.

I'm in Act 4 and this game is dropping an amazing amount of white gear (what you wear for like an hour or two in Act 1). It's not even worth dropping...why is it even dropping??? I'm looking for INT mage type gear, but the game drops mostly STR gear. If I play a second playthrough, I'll have like 30-40 good blue/green pieces or gear. Annoying. Also, I would expect all bosses in Act 4 to at least drop one piece of green gear, but that rarely happens. I'll kill 7-8 bosses in a location and sometimes have absolutely nothing good drop that's even worth selling. Thankfully you make enough gold in the game to buy something half decent from merchants. This would be great for people who like spending all their time selling gear to merchants 2/3rds of their playthrough.

The fighting in this game is very finnicky and unresponsive at times. I've died a million times because my projectiles won't go where they are aiming. If I'm already shooting at a target and I try to hit another target I sometimes have to let go of all buttons on mice & keybord before aiming at new target and then press 'fire'. That's not fun.

Like me, the game feels quite dull and repetetive for long periods of time. I imaging going through all of this with another character, but it seems like that would be a chore. IDK, could be wrong.

With all that being said, if you've played all the other ARPG games like this one, go ahead and get it if it's on sale. It's the reason I got this game.

Игра впрочем неидеальная. На то есть пару серьезных или не очень недостатков:
1) Тут легко можно запороть свой билд. Если очки умений в школах прокачки ещё можно перераспределить (отдавая за это совсем уж небольшие деньги), то очки характеристик намертво закрепляются после того как ты их распределил между силой, ловкостью и интеллектом. В детстве я так испортил своего самого первого героя - Хозяина Стихий. Класс магический, заточенный под посохи, и который я по своей глупости одевал как милишника и тратил все очки в силу и ловкость. Хватило меня с таким билдом ненадолго, и даже осознав ошибку мне недохватало интеллекта в любом случае (как в реальности, так и на этом персе)
2) Очень маленькие хранилища. Если вы по натуре складировщик который хочет оставить красивые шмотки на будущее или другим персонажам, то приготовьтесь создавать других героев либо как носителей того барахла что вы раздобыли, либо как чистых складовщиков
3) Вещи. 90% всего лута что вам упадёт будет серого, белого или жёлтого качества. Первые два вы перестаёте носить на 2-м или 3-м уровне, а жёлтые предметы остаются лишь когда нечего одеть другого. Зелёные и салатовые предметы лучше, падают они... нормально, и это единственные чаще всего предметы куда вам стоит пихать свои реликвии собираемые по ходу прохождения. Of my currtent characters 29 deaths, 28 are because I accidently clicked down on the left stick (an action I cannot NOT do durring tense moments) and swapped weapons leading to instadeath.  I may have to get 2 sets of the same weapons (or similar) and just set up the other half the same.  There's no remapping controller hotkeys.  Anyway... Enough complaining - It's a great game and unlike most other ARPG's ... you're not saddled with a super slow run/walk speed at all. In fact, you can even turn the game speed up!
